<Note>
  <strong>Prerequisite</strong><br />
  You need an active workspace and application. Start with [Create Your First Feature](/docs/build/quick-start).
</Note>

Every Build output should be reviewed like production engineering work. Revolte prepares the implementation and pull request, but your team decides whether the change is correct, maintainable, and safe to merge.

## Why review matters

AI-generated work can move quickly, but speed is only useful when the output is traceable. Reviewing the pull request confirms that the implementation matches the requirement and does not introduce hidden behavior, insecure defaults, or deployment surprises.

## What Revolte generates

A completed build can include:

- Source code changes
- Tests
- Documentation updates
- Configuration changes
- Pull request summary
- Validation logs

## Review workflow

<Steps>
  <Step title="Check the requirement match">
    Compare the pull request against the original request. Confirm the generated behavior solves the actual problem.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Inspect the code">
    Review the diff for correctness, maintainability, existing conventions, security-sensitive paths, and unnecessary abstractions.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Validate tests">
    Confirm tests cover success paths, invalid inputs, permission failures, empty states, and integration boundaries.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Review configuration">
    Check any environment variables, service changes, branch mappings, or deployment-related updates.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Approve or refine">
    Merge only when the output is ready. If not, provide precise feedback and let Revolte update the pull request.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Review checklist

| Area | Questions to ask |
| --- | --- |
| Requirement | Does the change satisfy the requested behavior? |
| Scope | Did Revolte avoid unrelated edits? |
| Code | Does it follow existing architecture and style? |
| Tests | Are important edge cases covered? |
| Config | Are required variables and secrets accounted for? |
| Deploy | Is the deployment impact clear? |

## Example review feedback

Use specific feedback so the next iteration is actionable.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Good feedback">
    ```txt
    Update the generated endpoint to return 403 for authenticated users without the admin role. Add a test for that case and keep the existing 401 behavior for missing tokens.
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Weak feedback">
    ```txt
    This is not right. Fix auth.
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Merge checklist

- Requirement is satisfied
- Tests pass
- Generated documentation is accurate
- Config and secrets are accounted for
- The pull request is approved by the right owner
- Deployment impact is understood

> **After merge**  
> Continue with [Deploy Your Application](/docs/deploy/quick-start) to release the approved change.
